answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: every agent must lock real collateral before it can act, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs as much as buying a glacier of tokens. Reputation accrues only through verifiable on-chain work, letting trust bloom like a violet that cannot be faked overnight. New identities enter through a nebula of probation, rate-limited and graded by independent peers, so a swarm of fresh accounts can never outvote established ones without enormous expense. This makes attacks economically irrational, not merely detectable.
